clue.text: Suffering this year from psychiatric disorder

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so the words beside it are knocked out of their proper order

parts.note: two words taken as written, all eight letters used

explanation.surface: Someone has had a bad year because of a mental illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The disorder in the surface is the definition, and the letters of 'this year' rearrange to give HYSTERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria was long classed as a psychiatric condition marked by uncontrolled emotional outbursts.

clue.text: Some think no better bit of butter can be found

indicators.note: only some of the following words is wanted, so the letters lie inside the run of text

parts.note: the letters run across the end of think, all of no and the start of better

explanation.surface: Some people reckon nothing beats a little butter.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across thinK NO Better.
explanation.definitionFit: A knob of butter is the usual phrase for a small lump of it, cut off for cooking.

clue.text: With a will unopened, what's left in it?

indicators.note: not opened means the opening, the first letter, is taken away

parts.note: a person dying testate has made a valid will

explanation.surface: A question about what remains to be shared out once a will is read.
explanation.walkthrough: TESTATE loses its first letter T to leave ESTATE; the definition refers back to the will just mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead person's estate is all the property and money they leave behind, which a will disposes of.

clue.text: Reliable tool hoisted in the beginning

indicators.note: in tells us the tool sits inside the other word
in a down clue, hoisting lifts the word upward so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an awl is a pointed tool for piercing leather or wood

explanation.surface: A dependable implement lifted at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: An awl is a pointed tool for piercing leather; in a down entry 'hoisted' turns it upside down before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart supporter is loyal and dependable, someone who can be relied on.

clue.text: Do your bit, being sorry about second-rate turn

indicators.note: about means going round, so the remorseful word wraps the other letters

explanation.surface: Pitch in, even though you're ashamed of your poor performance.
explanation.walkthrough: B and U go inside CONTRITE: CONTRI-BU-TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To contribute is to give your share to a joint effort, which is doing your bit.

clue.text: An ape's ill, missing a rabbit

indicators.note: missing tells us the word ill is taken out of the ape

parts.note: taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: An ape is sick and a rabbit has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill' looks like a description of the ape, but it is the very letters removed from the ape's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angora is a breed of domestic rabbit prized for its long, soft wool.

clue.text: Gainsay headmaster reorganising schools

indicators.note: reorganising puts things into a new arrangement, so these letters are shuffled
the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of master is kept

parts.note: the head of master, its first letter

explanation.surface: A headteacher who objects to a restructuring of schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headmaster' reads as one person but splits into head plus master, giving just M.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnasia is the plural of gymnasium, the name for an academic secondary school in Germany and elsewhere.

clue.text: Post in the form of an omen

parts.note: as means in the role or form of
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: Mail arriving that looks like a portent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a noun for mail, but it is the verb meaning to station someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To post someone somewhere is to assign them to a job or place of duty.

clue.text: It's difficult to get model aroused

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: Getting a model in the mood is hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: Model T is the classic Ford car, a common crossword source of T.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny problem is a tricky, awkward one, as full of snags as a briar.

clue.text: End of Guinness barrel, or of cigarette

definitions.note: read with 'End of' from the start of the clue: the end of a cigarette

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only the close of the drink's name is kept

parts.note: a tub is a barrel-like container

explanation.surface: The dregs of a keg of stout, or a cigarette end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' works twice: it picks the last letter of Guinness, and with 'or of cigarette' it gives the definition, the butt left after smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is the short remaining stump of a cigarette after it has been smoked.

clue.text: Washing over — consequently gain forgiveness

indicators.note: a word lying over another covers it, so one goes round the other

parts.note: ablutions are acts of washing oneself

explanation.surface: Ritual washing brings pardon for sins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washing over' reads as a phrase, but over is the signal for one word covering another.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is the formal release from guilt or sin, especially as granted by a priest.

clue.text: Rig out for soiree of sorrow

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the three letters are reshuffled

parts.note: a soiree is an evening do, from French soir; eve is the old word for evening

explanation.surface: Kitting someone out for a sad evening party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rig out' looks like dressing up, but out is the shuffle signal on rig.
explanation.definitionFit: To grieve and to sorrow are both verbs for feeling deep sadness, especially after a loss.

clue.text: Free terrorists snap title up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the string is read from the bottom toward the top

parts.note: ETA was the Basque separatist group
a snap is a photo, a pic

explanation.surface: Militants release a photo that gives away a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb to set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To emancipate is to set someone free from slavery or other restraint.

clue.text: Solemn air of old king rolling species of cannabis

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so the plant name is read backwards

parts.note: Cannabis sativa is the best-known species

explanation.surface: A stoned former monarch with an unlikely look of dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: GR, for Georgius Rex, appears on old coins and postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravitas is dignified seriousness of manner, the weighty bearing of someone to be taken seriously.

clue.text: Farewell to artist returning to the mountain

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the whole string runs backwards

explanation.surface: Waving off a painter who heads back to the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta-ra is a northern English cheerio; RA is a member of the Royal Academy. The first 'to' belongs to the wordplay's joining.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ararat in Turkey is the peak where Noah's Ark came to rest, hence the mountain.

clue.text: What's got into a parasite at the pub?

indicators.note: something that has got into another is now inside it

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

explanation.surface: Asking what's bitten a person in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has': EH has got into A LOUSE, A-L-EH-OUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is an old word for a tavern or public house serving beer.

clue.text: Dined, consuming barrel of pitch properly

indicators.note: consuming takes something in, so the meal word swallows the cask

parts.note: a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: Someone ate, and drank down a whole cask too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barrel of pitch' tempts one to think of a tar barrel; pitch belongs to the musical definition instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To attune an instrument is to bring it into tune, setting its pitch correctly.

clue.text: Immortal carrying Cross inside and outside

indicators.note: a word carrying another holds it within itself

explanation.surface: A god bearing a crucifix within and without.
explanation.walkthrough: X goes inside ETERNAL after the E. 'Inside and outside' looks like one phrase, but only 'outside' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: External describes what is on the outer surface or comes from outside.

clue.text: Helpless dairymaid raised a great many

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the remaining letters are read upward
less means without, so the word for help is taken away

parts.note: help is aid, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A defenceless milkmaid brought up a large brood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helpless' reads as one adjective, but it splits as help plus less, a removal instruction on the maid's own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Myriad means countless or a vast number, from the Greek for ten thousand.

clue.text: China has many an ornamental garden

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword's many
a rockery is a garden of stones and alpines

explanation.surface: The country of China boasts a number of decorative gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain tableware.
explanation.definitionFit: Crockery is plates, cups and dishes, and china is the fine porcelain kind.

clue.text: Initially rock hard, yet the Hammersmith Mauler gets beat

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each following word

parts.words: rock hard, yet the Hammersmith Mauler
parts.note: first letters of these six words

explanation.surface: A tough boxer nicknamed after a London district gets punched.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hammersmith Mauler is an invented boxer's nickname; Hammersmith is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical beat is the regular pulse that makes up the rhythm of a piece.

clue.text: A case of silence stifling passion

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the hush wraps round the feeling

explanation.surface: An example of feelings being kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A case of' looks like 'an instance of', but 'A case' is the definition and 'of' the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting case, as for a knife or sword blade.

clue.text: Belt encircling a tyrant

indicators.note: encircling means going all round, so the belt holds the letter

explanation.surface: A strap fastened round a despot.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a Persian provincial governor, and the word now means a petty despot.

clue.text: Soda-server is absorbing Mahler's First and Tchaikovsky's (or one of their ilk)

indicators.note: absorbing takes something in, so the soda device holds a letter

parts.note: a soda syphon dispenses fizzy water

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of each composer's name

explanation.surface: A soda dispenser apparently soaking up the music of two great composers.
explanation.walkthrough: Mahler and Tchaikovsky are both famed for their symphonies, so the definition points back at them; 'First' serves both names.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphonist is a composer of symphonies, as Mahler and Tchaikovsky were.

clue.text: Animal utterance involving trunk?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the sound a dog makes
second meaning: the rough outer covering of a tree

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests an elephant's trumpeting, but it is the trunk of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the cry of a dog and the tough outer layer covering a tree's stem.

clue.text: Live without a seaman's doll

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the verb sits round the sailor

explanation.surface: Getting by without a sailor's toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but here it is the old sense outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe and doll are both slang terms for an attractive young woman or a sweetheart.

clue.text: Demonstrative about alien goddess

indicators.note: about means around, so the pointing word goes round the visitor

explanation.surface: An emotional person talks about a deity from another world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstrative' looks like emotionally open, but it is the grammar term for words like this and that.
explanation.definitionFit: Thetis was a sea nymph of Greek myth, mother of Achilles, often counted a goddess.

clue.text: Overcome by exhaustion, so debated a treatment

indicators.note: a treatment works something over, so these letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Worn out after arguing a medical therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treatment' looks like medical care, but it is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead beat is an informal phrase meaning utterly worn out, completely tired.
